# Code review: Glyphbound, changes after the owner's first play-test (read-only)

You are the second-opinion reviewer for **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter in Unreal Engine 5.9.0 (C++), made for a 4-day game jam. Do not modify any file. Do not build or run anything.

## Context
- Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (short). The design is in `Design/GDD.md`; the changelog entry v0.14 at the top lists what the owner asked for after playing the first build.
- The change under review is everything between git commit `798a4e5` and `HEAD` (`git diff 798a4e5 HEAD --stat`, then read the files). It was written by four AI implementers in parallel (reports in `Prompts/feedback1_notes.md`) and then compiled and integrated by a fifth. It builds, the tests pass and a scripted smoke run passes, so a missing include is NOT what we want from you.
- Code: `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/`. Data: `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`.
- Engine source for checking APIs: `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source`.

## What changed (review these areas)
1. **Owned weapons** (`Weapons/GBEquipmentComponent.*`, `World/GBPickup.*`, `World/GBChest.cpp`, `Items/GBInventoryComponent.cpp`, `World/GBProgressSubsystem.h`): a picked-up weapon joins the owned list and goes to the hands only if its slot is empty; the player equips owned weapons from the Weapons page of the inventory. Ammo and element of stored weapons must survive swaps, checkpoints, death and era travel.
2. **Held ice shield** (`Spells/GBSpell_Shield.*`, `Spells/GBSpellbookComponent.*`, `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.*`, `Player/GBInputSet.*`): the spell summons a shield for a duration; the Block input (Q / L2, hold) raises it; only a raised shield blocks, and only from the front. Look for: the shield blocking when lowered, never expiring, surviving death or era travel wrongly, the move-speed modifier left on after it ends, blocking while a menu is open, the L2 conflict with the spell modifier on gamepad.
3. **Mouse in menus** (`Player/GBPlayerController.*`, `UI/GBHUD*.cpp`): cursor shown in menus, click handling through hit rects, input mode switched on open / close. Look for: the cursor or the UI input mode left on after closing a menu or after death / respawn, a click acting twice, clicks acting on a stale hit rect of a previous frame or menu, the game staying paused.
4. **Kill-Z** (`Core/GBGameMode.*`, `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.*`, `AI/GBEnemyCharacter.*`): falling below `KillZ` kills the player (once) and enemies (through the attribute component so encounters progress).
5. **Damage numbers** (`UI/GBHUD_DamageNumbers.cpp`, `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.*` global event): look for delegate lifetime problems (HUD destroyed and still bound, bound twice after a respawn), unbounded growth, numbers for the player's own damage taken.
6. **Explosions and textured structures** (`Combat/GBExplosionEffect.*`, `Combat/GBProjectile.*`, `Spells/GBSpell_Projectile.*`, `Spells/GBSpell_Wall.*`, `Core/GBPlaceholder.cpp`, `UI/GBPixelSpriteLibrary.*`, `Tools/Jam/make_materials.py`): every projectile explosion path must spawn the shockwave exactly once and never damage twice; knockback only on hostile characters; the material `/Game/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelSurface` must load in a packaged build (see `Glyphbound/Config/DefaultGame.ini`) and missing-material fallbacks must not crash.
7. **Enemy pathing** (`AI/GBSteering.*`, `AI/GBEnemyCharacter.*`, `World/GBTestArena.*`, `Config/DefaultEngine.ini`): navmesh built at runtime plus a local steering fallback and a stuck check. Look for: state machine dead ends (an enemy that can never attack because of the new line-of-sight rule, e.g. the trace hitting its own capsule, the player's shield, another enemy or an era-hidden prop), steering toward ledges, timers never reset, enemies frozen after era travel.

## What to report (real defects only, most severe first)
- Runtime bugs a player would hit, state that leaks between death / respawn / era travel / menus, and contract breaks between the modules above.
- Data and code mismatches: a key in a JSON file that the code spells differently or never reads, and the reverse.
- Things that work in the Editor but break in a packaged build.
- Real balance numbers hardcoded where data should decide.

Do not report: style, naming, formatting, missing comments, micro-optimizations, multiplayer issues (single player), or the number of tests.

## Output format
A numbered list, most severe first, at most 20 items. For each:
- `file:line` (or lines),
- what is wrong, in one or two sentences,
- why it matters when playing (what the player would see),
- the smallest fix you would make.
Finish with one short paragraph: the three things you would fix first, and anything you checked and found solid.

1	# Day 1: 2026-11-12
2	
3	> Architect's entry, written by the AI architect (Claude Code) as the day went. A person on the team reviews it and adds the human side (play-test notes, their own screenshots) starting from `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`. **Nobody has played the build yet**: everything below was checked by compiling, by the automated tests and by a scripted run of the game, not by a person.
4	
5	## Summary in 3 lines
6	- The owner set the vision and the rules and left; the AI architect took every technical decision alone and built the project "Glyphbound" from an empty folder (UE 5.9.0, C++, no template gameplay).
7	- The whole code structure of the game was laid out in one pass: the architect wrote the header contracts, ten AI implementers filled them in parallel (17,500 lines), and the first compile of all of it had **three** errors.
8	- A second model reviewed the code and found 9 real defects; a scripted run of the game found two more that no compiler or reviewer saw (no floor under the player; magenta sprites). All fixed the same day.
9	
10	## Goal of the day vs. result
11	| Goal | Result | Evidence (commit, screenshot, clip) |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| Create the UE 5.9.0 project with unused plugins off, measure Editor boot before and after | Done | commit `8034a7c`, numbers below |
14	| First-person controller (move, jump, double jump, dash) | Built; the scripted run shows the player standing in the arena. Feel not checked by a person yet | `3b3e6e3`, `e9102fc` |
15	| Pixel-art hands (placeholder) | Done: hands and staff are pixel sprites described as text | `media/2026-11-12/2_past_gun.png` |
16	| Staff with basic magic attack + a gun, with switching | Done (plus shotgun, rifle and the sword as data) | `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png`, `2_past_gun.png` |
17	| One spell, 100% data-driven, ready to scale with the QTE | Exceeded: the 13 spells of the GDD as data on 8 reusable behaviors, and a first QTE | `media/2026-11-12/6_qte.png` |
18	| Health and mana with regeneration | Done | HUD in every screenshot |
19	| A portal that swaps past and future with a fade, in a test map | Done: test arena built in code, two looks, era-gated room and a past-to-future unlock | `media/2026-11-12/8_respawn.png` |
20	| Packaged build | Done: Win64 zip, 245.3 MB; the packaged exe passes the scripted run | `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` (not in git), commit of this entry |
21	
22	Beyond the day-1 target, a first version of these also exists (GDD days 2-3): enemies and wave encounters, inventory with consumables, armor and recipes, both skill trees, the two HUD skins, checkpoints and death.
23	
24	## How we used AI today
25	| Agent / tool | Model | What for | Result | Log |
26	|---|---|---|---|---|
27	| Claude Code (architect) | Claude Fable 5.2 | Read the GDD, took the technical decisions, created the project, wrote every public header (the contracts), split the work, reviewed the reports, decided each fix, wrote the build / test / smoke tooling | Project, architecture, tooling, this entry | `raw/CENTRAL/2026-11-12/claude-…` |
28	| Claude Code subagents (10 in parallel) | Claude Opus 5.5, effort High | One implementer per code folder: data + stats, combat, player, weapons, spells, QTE, world, enemies, items + skills, UI | 103 files, about 17,500 lines, written without compiling (they were forbidden to build: ten builds at once on one machine would have fought each other) | same session log (subagent transcripts) |
29	| OpenCode | Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor, High | Serial work: (1) the integration pass that made it compile and pass the tests; (2) the batch of fixes after the review | Both green on the first try | `raw/CENTRAL/2026-11-12/agents/*opencode*` |
30	| Codex CLI | GPT Sol 6.1, Medium | Second opinion: read-only review of the combat core, data-vs-code mismatches and packaged-build risks | 9 findings, all real, all fixed | `raw/CENTRAL/2026-11-12/agents/*codex*` |
31	
32	**Prompt of the day** (the owner's instruction to the architect, written in Spanish; English translation below):
33	```
34	Quiero que hagas one shot de toda la base del proyecto. Los hechizos tienen que ser modulares y tienen que poder
35	ajustarse todos sus parámetros. [...] Y la codebase es literalmente tuya. Es tu responsabilidad que quede lo mejor
36	posible y tú eres el dueño de todas las decisiones sobre el código.
37	```
38	> "I want you to one-shot the whole base of the project. Spells must be modular and every one of their parameters must be adjustable. [...] And the codebase is literally yours. It is your responsibility to make it as good as possible, and you own every decision about the code."
39	
40	This is the theme (DIRECTOR'S CUT) applied to the process: the owner sets the vision and walks away; the AI directs the other AIs and decides what makes the cut.
41	
42	**What the AI did well**
43	- **Contracts before code.** The architect wrote every public header first, with the specification in the comments, and checked that they pass Unreal's header tool. Ten implementers then worked at the same time without seeing each other's code. Result of the first full compile: 3 errors in 17,500 lines (two name collisions between files that Unreal compiles together, one local variable hiding an engine member).
44	- **Implementers reported their own doubts.** Each one ended with a list of what it could not verify and what it needed from the others. Those lists became the checklist of the integration pass.
45	- **The reviewer found design-level bugs, not typos.** Example: dying restored the inventory from the checkpoint while opened chests stayed open, so a death could delete rewards for good. The fix was a design decision (death now keeps everything collected), taken by the architect and written into the GDD.
46	
47	**Where the AI failed and how we fixed it** (the part judges value most in a dev log)
48	- **The game compiled, passed its tests, passed review, and had no floor.** The game mode builds the test arena "when the map has no player start"; the engine's empty map has one. So the player spawned in the void and fell forever. No compiler, no unit test and neither reviewing model caught it. It was caught by `gb.Smoke`, a console command the architect wrote because AI agents are not allowed to run Play In Editor here: it runs the game by itself, uses the main systems on a timer, logs what happens, takes screenshots and quits. The first run printed the player's height: -1,140 cm, then -10,992 cm. The script now fails when the player falls or the level has no enemies.
49	- **Magenta hands.** The placeholder sprites are text: rows of letters and a palette. The implementer used `s` for skin and `S` for shadow. Unreal's string keys ignore case, so one of the two colors was lost and those pixels were drawn in the "missing" color. Seen only in the screenshots. Fixed with a script that renames colliding keys to digits; the rule is now in the data header.
50	- **Works in the Editor, breaks in the package.** The arena code called `ADirectionalLight::GetComponent()`, which only exists in Editor builds. The Editor build was green; the first packaging failed. Fixed, and the game target is now built on every integration, not only when packaging.
51	- **The plugin diet broke the package.** Among the 103 default plugins the architect turned off was Cascade, the old particle system, which the game does not use. The engine's own renderer settings still look up two console variables that only that plugin registers; the Editor shrugs, but the cook counts the two log errors and fails. Cascade is back on (102 plugins off), with the reason written next to the list in `Tools/Jam/trim_plugins.js`. Lesson: "the game does not use it" is not the same as "the engine does not need it", and only packaging tells.
52	- **The architect's own slip:** a "commit everything" swept two files that the integration agent was still editing into a commit labeled as a design change. Harmless, but the history is slightly mislabeled there (`1fad33f`). Since then, commits made while an agent is working name their paths.
53	- **A measurement that showed nothing.** See "Problems".
54	
55	## Design decisions
56	All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering. The provisional gameplay rules and numbers that had to be invented are listed in GDD section 18 for the owner to confirm or change.
57	
58	- **C++ only, built from the blank template.** The first-person template was not used: the jam asks for gameplay beyond Epic's templates, and AI agents handle C++ text far better than Blueprint graphs.
59	- **No Gameplay Ability System.** Considered (the GDD lists it as a candidate) and rejected: heavy boilerplate and asset setup for a 4-day jam. Replaced by three small pieces we fully control: one stat system (base value from data + stacked modifiers), one damage function, one status-effect component. Skill-tree nodes, armor, slows, potions, air passives and the weapon enchant are all "a named group of modifiers".
60	- **All gameplay numbers in JSON under `Content/Data`, shipped as loose files.** Git only carries text in this team, AI agents edit text reliably, and the owner can retune a packaged build with a text editor. `gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing.
61	- **Spells = data + a behavior class.** Each parameter has `Base / Min / Max / ScaledBy` (none, QTE power, QTE reach). Eight behaviors cover the nine active spells and the enchant; a new spell that fits a behavior is one JSON entry.
62	- **No binary assets needed to run.** The test arena, input actions and placeholders are built in C++; placeholder pixel art is rows of text turned into textures at runtime. The whole game is reviewable as text in git.
63	- **HUD drawn with the canvas, not widgets.** The two skins (90s RPG with the staff, cyberpunk with a gun) are two style structs.
64	- **Death keeps what was collected** (after the review): back to the checkpoint's place with full health, mana and ammo; nothing owned is rolled back.
65	- **Modifier keys by weapon type** (`Weapon.Gun.*`), added after the review found the gun enchant also buffed the staff.
66	- **Routing of work between models** (owner's rule): parallel work to Claude subagents, one-batch-at-a-time work to Muse Spark, reviews to Codex.
67	- **Exceptions to "the implementer is Muse Spark"**, with the reason: the project scaffold, the header contracts and the build / test / smoke scripts were written by the architect directly (they are the architecture and its verification); two one-line fixes and the sprite palette script were also direct (smaller than the prompt that would describe them).
68	
69	## Assets created
70	| Asset | Tool (AI or manual) | Prompt or source | License | Machine |
71	|---|---|---|---|---|
72	| 36 placeholder pixel sprites (`Content/Data/Sprites.json`, rows of text) | AI (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent "UI") | Architect's task brief in the session log | Own work | CENTRAL |
73	
74	No third-party assets. Engine content used: the basic shapes and engine materials that ship with UE 5.9.
75	
76	## Problems and solutions
77	- **Trimming plugins did not speed up a warm Editor boot.** We expected a gain; measured, there is none worth the name. Mounted plugins went from 315 to 160, warm boot stayed around 10-11 s. The cost of a warm boot is not in the plugin count. We keep the trimmed list (fewer modules to load and cook) and spent no more time on it.
78	- **Screenshots arrive late.** The engine captures a screenshot a few frames after the request, so in the first smoke run a shot of "the future" showed the inventory that opened right after. The script now leaves a full second after each shot.
79	- Everything else is in "Where the AI failed" above.
80	
81	## Screenshots / clips
82	All taken by the scripted run (`gb.Smoke`), not by a person playing.
83	- `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png`: the past. Staff in hand, 90s RPG HUD, an ice wall just cast.
84	- `media/2026-11-12/2_past_gun.png`: pixel-art hands holding the 3D pistol, cyberpunk HUD, the gun enchanted with fire.
85	- `media/2026-11-12/3_future_gun.png`: the same place in the future (dark, neon).
86	- `media/2026-11-12/4_inventory.png`, `5_skills.png`: inventory and both skill trees, each tree in its own style.
87	- `media/2026-11-12/6_qte.png`: the spell QTE: key sequence, time bar, power and reach.
88	- `media/2026-11-12/7_death.png`, `8_respawn.png`: death screen and the respawn at the portal, keeping the learned spells.
89	
90	## Numbers of the day
91	- Editor boot, `Total Editor Startup Time` from the log (same machine, same code, empty startup map):
92	
93	| Plugin set | Mounted plugins | Cold (first boot) | Warm boots |
94	|---|---|---|---|
95	| Default + `AllToolsets` (baseline) | 315 | 37.9 s | 10.97 s, 10.96 s |
96	| Trimmed (18 toolsets, 103 defaults off; later 102, see above) | 160 | 16.3 s (first boot after the change) | 10.09 s, 11.15 s |
97	
98	- Code: 103 files, about 17,500 lines; 11 JSON data files.
99	- First full compile of all the parallel work: 3 errors.
100	- Tests: 22 pure-logic tests, 0.35 s of test time, 15-25 s wall time with the Editor boot.
101	- Smoke run: 25 steps, about 38 s wall time.
102	- Build times: first build of the empty module 55 s; incremental builds 2-26 s.
103	- Package: `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`, **245.3 MB** (the jam asks for under 1 GB), built in 56 s once the cook was fixed. The packaged exe passes the same scripted run, reading the JSON data as loose files next to it.
104	- Agent sessions / prompts / external agent runs / MCP calls / commits: see `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`.
105	
106	## Tools used so far (for the submission's "Tools you used" field)
107	Unreal Engine 5.9.0, Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5), OpenCode (Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor), Codex CLI (GPT Sol 6.1), Unreal Editor MCP server (boot measurements only), git.
108	
109	## Plan for tomorrow
110	- A person plays the packaged build first, and their notes decide the order of everything else.
111	- Tune by playing: movement feel, mouse gesture sensitivity in the QTE, gun viewmodel size, spell numbers.
112	- GDD day 2: gamepad pass, enemy behavior and one real wave, consumables in play, QTE second version, DLSS plugin check for the NVIDIA award.
113	- Replace placeholders as art arrives from the other machines.

> "I want you to one-shot the whole base of the project. Spells must be modular and every one of their parameters must be adjustable. [...] And the codebase is literally yours. It is your responsibility to make it as good as possible, and you own every decision about the code."

This is the theme (DIRECTOR'S CUT) applied to the process: the owner sets the vision and walks away; the AI directs the other AIs and decides what makes the cut.

**What the AI did well**
- **Contracts before code.** The architect wrote every public header first, with the specification in the comments, and checked that they pass Unreal's header tool. Ten implementers then worked at the same time without seeing each other's code. Result of the first full compile: 3 errors in 17,500 lines (two name collisions between files that Unreal compiles together, one local variable hiding an engine member).
- **Implementers reported their own doubts.** Each one ended with a list of what it could not verify and what it needed from the others. Those lists became the checklist of the integration pass.
- **The reviewer found design-level bugs, not typos.** Example: dying restored the inventory from the checkpoint while opened chests stayed open, so a death could delete rewards for good. The fix was a design decision (death now keeps everything collected), taken by the architect and written into the GDD.

**Where the AI failed and how we fixed it** (the part judges value most in a dev log)
- **The game compiled, passed its tests, passed review, and had no floor.** The game mode builds the test arena "when the map has no player start"; the engine's empty map has one. So the player spawned in the void and fell forever. No compiler, no unit test and neither reviewing model caught it. It was caught by `gb.Smoke`, a console command the architect wrote because AI agents are not allowed to run Play In Editor here: it runs the game by itself, uses the main systems on a timer, logs what happens, takes screenshots and quits. The first run printed the player's height: -1,140 cm, then -10,992 cm. The script now fails when the player falls or the level has no enemies.
- **Magenta hands.** The placeholder sprites are text: rows of letters and a palette. The implementer used `s` for skin and `S` for shadow. Unreal's string keys ignore case, so one of the two colors was lost and those pixels were drawn in the "missing" color. Seen only in the screenshots. Fixed with a script that renames colliding keys to digits; the rule is now in the data header.
- **Works in the Editor, breaks in the package.** The arena code called `ADirectionalLight::GetComponent()`, which only exists in Editor builds. The Editor build was green; the first packaging failed. Fixed, and the game target is now built on every integration, not only when packaging.
- **The plugin diet broke the package.** Among the 103 default plugins the architect turned off was Cascade, the old particle system, which the game does not use. The engine's own renderer settings still look up two console variables that only that plugin registers; the Editor shrugs, but the cook counts the two log errors and fails. Cascade is back on (102 plugins off), with the reason written next to the list in `Tools/Jam/trim_plugins.js`. Lesson: "the game does not use it" is not the same as "the engine does not need it", and only packaging tells.
- **The architect's own slip:** a "commit everything" swept two files that the integration agent was still editing into a commit labeled as a design change. Harmless, but the history is slightly mislabeled there (`1fad33f`). Since then, commits made while an agent is working name their paths.
- **A measurement that showed nothing.** See "Problems".

## Design decisions
All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering. The provisional gameplay rules and numbers that had to be invented are listed in GDD section 18 for the owner to confirm or change.

- **C++ only, built from the blank template.** The first-person template was not used: the jam asks for gameplay beyond Epic's templates, and AI agents handle C++ text far better than Blueprint graphs.
- **No Gameplay Ability System.** Considered (the GDD lists it as a candidate) and rejected: heavy boilerplate and asset setup for a 4-day jam. Replaced by three small pieces we fully control: one stat system (base value from data + stacked modifiers), one damage function, one status-effect component. Skill-tree nodes, armor, slows, potions, air passives and the weapon enchant are all "a named group of modifiers".
- **All gameplay numbers in JSON under `Content/Data`, shipped as loose files.** Git only carries text in this team, AI agents edit text reliably, and the owner can retune a packaged build with a text editor. `gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing.
- **Spells = data + a behavior class.** Each parameter has `Base / Min / Max / ScaledBy` (none, QTE power, QTE reach). Eight behaviors cover the nine active spells and the enchant; a new spell that fits a behavior is one JSON entry.
- **No binary assets needed to run.** The test arena, input actions and placeholders are built in C++; placeholder pixel art is rows of text turned into textures at runtime. The whole game is reviewable as text in git.
- **HUD drawn with the canvas, not widgets.** The two skins (90s RPG with the staff, cyberpunk with a gun) are two style structs.
- **Death keeps what was collected** (after the review): back to the checkpoint's place with full health, mana and ammo; nothing owned is rolled back.
- **Modifier keys by weapon type** (`Weapon.Gun.*`), added after the review found the gun enchant also buffed the staff.
- **Routing of work between models** (owner's rule): parallel work to Claude subagents, one-batch-at-a-time work to Muse Spark, reviews to Codex.
- **Exceptions to "the implementer is Muse Spark"**, with the reason: the project scaffold, the header contracts and the build / test / smoke scripts were written by the architect directly (they are the architecture and its verification); two one-line fixes and the sprite palette script were also direct (smaller than the prompt that would describe them).

## Assets created
| Asset | Tool (AI or manual) | Prompt or source | License | Machine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 36 placeholder pixel sprites (`Content/Data/Sprites.json`, rows of text) | AI (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent "UI") | Architect's task brief in the session log | Own work | CENTRAL |

No third-party assets. Engine content used: the basic shapes and engine materials that ship with UE 5.9.

## Problems and solutions
- **Trimming plugins did not speed up a warm Editor boot.** We expected a gain; measured, there is none worth the name. Mounted plugins went from 315 to 160, warm boot stayed around 10-11 s. The cost of a warm boot is not in the plugin count. We keep the trimmed list (fewer modules to load and cook) and spent no more time on it.
- **Screenshots arrive late.** The engine captures a screenshot a few frames after the request, so in the first smoke run a shot of "the future" showed the inventory that opened right after. The script now leaves a full second after each shot.
- Everything else is in "Where the AI failed" above.

## Screenshots / clips
All taken by the scripted run (`gb.Smoke`), not by a person playing.
- `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png`: the past. Staff in hand, 90s RPG HUD, an ice wall just cast.
- `media/2026-11-12/2_past_gun.png`: pixel-art hands holding the 3D pistol, cyberpunk HUD, the gun enchanted with fire.
- `media/2026-11-12/3_future_gun.png`: the same place in the future (dark, neon).
- `media/2026-11-12/4_inventory.png`, `5_skills.png`: inventory and both skill trees, each tree in its own style.
- `media/2026-11-12/6_qte.png`: the spell QTE: key sequence, time bar, power and reach.
- `media/2026-11-12/7_death.png`, `8_respawn.png`: death screen and the respawn at the portal, keeping the learned spells.

## Numbers of the day
- Editor boot, `Total Editor Startup Time` from the log (same machine, same code, empty startup map):

| Plugin set | Mounted plugins | Cold (first boot) | Warm boots |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default + `AllToolsets` (baseline) | 315 | 37.9 s | 10.97 s, 10.96 s |
| Trimmed (18 toolsets, 103 defaults off; later 102, see above) | 160 | 16.3 s (first boot after the change) | 10.09 s, 11.15 s |

- Code: 103 files, about 17,500 lines; 11 JSON data files.
- First full compile of all the parallel work: 3 errors.
- Tests: 22 pure-logic tests, 0.35 s of test time, 15-25 s wall time with the Editor boot.
- Smoke run: 25 steps, about 38 s wall time.
- Build times: first build of the empty module 55 s; incremental builds 2-26 s.
- Package: `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`, **245.3 MB** (the jam asks for under 1 GB), built in 56 s once the cook was fixed. The packaged exe passes the same scripted run, reading the JSON data as loose files next to it.
- Agent sessions / prompts / external agent runs / MCP calls / commits: see `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`.

## Tools used so far (for the submission's "Tools you used" field)
Unreal Engine 5.9.0, Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5), OpenCode (Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor), Codex CLI (GPT Sol 6.1), Unreal Editor MCP server (boot measurements only), git.

## Plan for tomorrow
- A person plays the packaged build first, and their notes decide the order of everything else.
- Tune by playing: movement feel, mouse gesture sensitivity in the QTE, gun viewmodel size, spell numbers.
- GDD day 2: gamepad pass, enemy behavior and one real wave, consumables in play, QTE second version, DLSS plugin check for the NVIDIA award.
- Replace placeholders as art arrives from the other machines.

## Second block: the owner plays the build and sends notes
The owner played the first packaged build and came back with ten notes, in Spanish, in one message and two follow-ups. This is the director's side of the theme: the vision is corrected by playing, not by reading code.

| Owner's note (translated) | What was done |
|---|---|
| "The ice wall has to be a 3D object with 2D textures, like the castle will be, because in the end it is a structure." | New art rule in the GDD: structures are never flat sprites. One generated material projects a pixel tile in world space with nearest filtering; the ice wall, and the past look of the whole test arena, use it. `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png` |
| "The fireball must have a shockwave / explosion even if it hits no enemy." | Every explosion path spawns a shockwave effect and pushes enemies back (knockback is data, scaled by QTE power). |
| "The double jump must be higher. Both jumps must be." | Jump velocity 620 -> 800 in `Player.json`; the arena's jump course is now computed from the player's data, so it stays valid when the number changes. |
| "On picking up a new staff, the old one must not stay on the floor: the new one goes to the inventory and the player equips it by hand." | Weapons are now owned; a pickup goes to the hands only if its slot is empty. New Weapons page in the inventory. Applied to guns and the sword too (provisional). |
| "The ice shield must work like a Skyrim shield: on a secondary key, raised by the player." | The spell summons the shield for a time; a new Block input (Q / L2, provisional) raises it. Only a raised shield blocks, from the front, and it slows the player. `media/2026-11-12/9_shield.png` |
| "Improve the enemy AI so they get around obstacles and do not just stand there." | A navmesh built at runtime over the code-built arena, plus a local steering fallback and a stuck check. The smoke run now puts an orc behind a wall and fails unless it reaches the player. |
| "On opening the skill tree the mouse is not visible." | Mouse support in every menu: cursor, hover, click on tabs, entries and skill nodes. |
| "When falling out of the map the player should die." | Kill height in `Game.json`, relative to the arena floor; enemies that fall die too, so their encounter moves on. |
| "Add damage numbers that come out of the enemy; bigger text when a hit is especially effective; rising, slightly random, fading." | Floating damage numbers driven by one global "damage dealt" event; big on headshots or hits of at least 25% of the target's health (provisional rule, data). |
| "Add one second to the QTE time." | `QTE.TimeLimit` 3 -> 4 in `QTE.json`. One line of data, no code. |

**How it was run.** Same pattern as the first block, smaller: the architect wrote the new public declarations, four Claude Opus subagents implemented in parallel (UI; weapons, shield and controller; structures and explosions; AI and arena), Muse Spark integrated, Codex reviewed.
- **The first compile of the four agents' work had zero errors** (48 files changed, about 4,400 lines added). The integration pass still had real work: the four reports listed five places where one agent's change needed a fix in a file nobody owned (for example, a click on the death screen respawned twice: the HUD agent and the controller agent had each handled it).
- **The riskiest piece worked on the first run:** the AI agent had to create a navigation mesh for a level that only exists in code. It read the engine source, found that a navigation volume spawned at runtime has no shape, and gave it one by hand. It said plainly in its report that this was "the main risk" and that it had never run it. The smoke run printed `navData=1` and the orc walked 1,757 cm around the wall in 3.9 s.

## Design decisions
All taken by the architect;

# Task: fixes after the review of the play-test 1 changes

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor. Do not commit.

A reviewer read the last change and found four defects; the architect decided each fix below and added a fifth item. Make exactly these changes, nothing else.

## 1. Line of sight must not pass through an allied enemy into cover
`AI/GBEnemyCharacter.cpp`, `HasLineOfSight` (around line 655): today, when the trace hits another enemy, it counts as a clear line. Wrong: a wall may be behind that enemy.
Fix: when the trace hits a pawn that is not the goal (another enemy), add it to the ignored actors and trace again from the same start, until the trace reaches the goal (clear), hits nothing (clear) or hits something that is not a pawn (blocked). Cap the loop at 8 repeats; if the cap is reached, the line is blocked.

## 2. Local steering must not walk off ledges
`AI/GBEnemyCharacter.cpp`, `SteerTowards` / `IsDirectionBlocked` (around lines 470-530): candidate directions are only checked for obstacles, never for ground, and the "boxed in" fallback steps backward unchecked.
Fix:
- A direction also counts as blocked when there is no walkable ground ahead: from the point `EnemySteerLedgeProbeDistance` cm along the direction (at the capsule's base height plus the step height), trace down `EnemySteerLedgeDrop` cm plus the step height against the same collision channel the capsule uses for the world, ignoring pawns; no hit, or a hit on a slope steeper than the walkable floor angle of the movement component, means no ground.
- New Game.json "Values" keys with those names (add them to `GBEnemyKey` like the others): `EnemySteerLedgeProbeDistance` 80, `EnemySteerLedgeDrop` 150.
- The backward fallback uses the same check (obstacle and ground); when it fails too, the enemy stays in place this tick (`StopMoving`), it does not move blind.
- Keep the pure function `GBSteering::ChooseOffset` unchanged (ledges just feed its `Blocked` array), so the existing test stays valid.
- The goal's own position never counts as a ledge when the goal is within the probe distance.

## 3. The Weapons page must show the weapon's real element
`UI/GBHUD_Menus.cpp` (around lines 1109 and 1126): the row and the details use `Def->Element`. Use `Equipment->GetWeaponElement(WeaponId)` in both places (a forged elemental sword must show its element).

## 4. Spell visuals that data defines must come from data
- **Raised shield in the HUD** (`UI/GBHUD.cpp`, `DrawRaisedShield`, around line 614): the sprite id is hardcoded to `ice_shield`. Read it from the active shield's spell definition: its "Strings" value `Sprite` (fallback `ice_shield`). Tint the sprite with the definition's `Color` string only through a NEW optional string `HudTint` ("#RRGGBB"; absent = white), so today's look does not change. Use the spellbook's `GetShieldActor()` and the spell actor's existing accessors for its definition / strings; do not add a second data lookup path if one exists.
- **Textured walls** (`Spells/GBSpell_Wall.cpp`, around line 65): the tint passed to `SetupTexturedShape` is always white. Read a NEW optional string `Tint` ("#RRGGBB"; absent = white). Do not use `Color` there (it is the plain-shape color and would darken the tile).
- In `Spells.json`, entry `IceShield`: remove the params / strings that nothing reads any more since the shield stopped being a world object (`SpriteSize`, `Distance` if no code reads them: check with a search first; keep `Sprite` and `Color`). Document `HudTint` and `Tint` in the header comments of `Spells/GBSpell_Shield.h` and `Spells/GBSpell_Wall.h` next to the other strings.

## 5. Smoke script: the shield screenshot is taken before the shield is on screen
`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`: the step "summon the ice shield, raise it, screenshot" raises the shield and asks for the screenshot in the same step, so the picture shows the first frame of the raise animation (shield still below the HUD panel). Split it: one step summons and raises (and logs `SMOKE shield cast=.. hasShield=.. raised=..`), a new step 0.7 s later takes the screenshot `9_shield`, and the "lower the shield" step runs at least 1.0 s after the screenshot. Shift the following steps accordingly and update the step count.

## Verification (all must be true when you finish)
1. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
2. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
3. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -MinTests 24` passes.
4. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1` ends with `Smoke: done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0 timedOut=False`, the line `SMOKE path check passed` is there, and no `LogGB` warning appears.
Never make an error disappear by deleting behavior. All JSON files stay valid.

## Final report (plain text)
1. The four result lines, copied verbatim, plus the `SMOKE path check end:` line.
2. What you changed per item, with file names.
3. Anything you could not do as described, and why.

## 18. Provisional rules and numbers picked by the architect (2026-11-12)
The owner asked the architect not to stop for missing design details. Everything below was chosen so the prototype could be built; **all of it is provisional** and waits for the owner's word. Numbers are in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and can be changed there without touching code.

### Rules
- **Double jump on day 1:** the player starts knowing the air passive "Double jump" so it can be tested now. In the real game it is learned in the air zone (§6); remove it from `Player.json` `StartingSpells` then.
- **Dash:** available from the start (the air passive only improves it). It goes in the movement direction (forward when standing still), works in the air, gives no invulnerability, and does not refill jumps.
- **Owning weapons:** decided by the owner for staffs (section 8): picked-up weapons go to the inventory and are equipped by hand. Provisional part: guns and the sword follow the same rule; each owned gun keeps its own ammo while stored.
- **Reload:** the bullets left in the old magazine are lost (classic tactical style). A gun reloads by itself when its magazine runs dry. Ammo pickups give one spare magazine, up to the gun's maximum.
- **Sustained spells (flamethrower):** after the QTE they run for their Duration, or until the same spell key is pressed again, the weapon is switched, or the player dies. Mana is paid once, at the start.
- **Ice shield QTE:** part 1 (power) scales its duration and health; part 2 (reach) scales how much frontal damage it blocks.
- **Modifier keys by weapon type:** besides one weapon (`Weapon.Pistol.Damage`) and all weapons (`Weapon.All.Damage`), a modifier can target a slot: `Weapon.Gun.*`, `Weapon.Staff.*`, `Weapon.Sword.*`. The enchant uses `Weapon.Gun.Damage`, so it never buffs the staff or the sword.
- **Explosions and enemy melee need a clear line** to their target: no damage through walls or through the ice wall.
- **Weapon enchant QTE:** part 1 scales how long the buff lasts; part 2 scales how strong it is. Only one enchant at a time. The enchanted gun deals the element's damage type and applies its effect on hit (fire burns, lightning shocks, ice chills).
- **Spell walls:** the fire wall does not block; it burns enemies that touch it. The ice wall blocks movement and shots and has health; anyone's shots can break it, the player's included. Enemies do not attack walls on purpose yet.

# Glyphbound: code architecture

> Written by the architect (Claude Code) on 2026-11-12. Source of truth for how the C++ is organized.
> Design lives in `Design/GDD.md`; this file says how the code implements it. Keep it short and current.

## Principles
1. **Data, not code.** Every gameplay number lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and is read through `UGBDataSubsystem`. Code never hardcodes damage, costs, speeds, durations, sizes or timings. The JSON ships as loose files, so numbers can be tuned in a packaged build with a text editor (`gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing).
2. **One stat system.** A number is a *named stat*: base value from data, then modifiers. `UGBStatsComponent` evaluates `(Base + adds) * multipliers` (or an override). Skill-tree nodes, armor, status effects, air passives and the weapon enchant are all just groups of modifiers with a source name. Nothing else changes numbers.
3. **One damage path.** Everything that hurts goes through `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage(Target, FGBDamageInfo)`. Shields, resistances, teams, on-hit effects and kill credit hook in there once.
4. **Spells are data + a behavior.** A spell is a `FGBSpellDefinition` (params with `Base/Min/Max/ScaledBy`) plus the class of an `AGBSpellActor` behavior. The QTE result (power, reach) scales the params tagged for it. A new spell that fits an existing behavior is a JSON entry, no code.
5. **Shared pieces.** One projectile (`AGBProjectile`) for staff bolts, spell projectiles, enemy shots and grenades. One status-effect component for slows, burns, potions and buffs. One interact interface for portals, chests, pickups and the seal.
6. **Text in git.** No binary assets are required to run: input actions, the test arena, placeholder shapes and placeholder pixel sprites are all built in C++ from text. `Content/` is ignored by git except `Content/Data/`.
7. **No GAS.** Unreal's Gameplay Ability System was considered and rejected for the jam: it needs a lot of boilerplate and asset setup, and the game's needs (costs, cooldowns, timed effects, stat upgrades) are covered by principles 2-4 in a few hundred lines we fully control.
8. **PIE is human-only.** Agents build, run the pure-logic tests and package; a person plays.

## Module layout (`Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound`, one runtime module, prefix `GB`)
Includes are relative to the module root: `#include "Stats/GBStatsComponent.h"`.

| Folder | What | Key types |
|---|---|---|
| `Core/` | Shared enums, stat names, placeholders (plain shapes and pixel-textured structures), game mode, dev commands | `GBTypes.h`, `GBStatNames.h`, `GBPlaceholder.h` (`SetupTexturedShape`), `AGBGameMode`, `UGBGameInstance`, `GBDevCommands.cpp` (`gb.Smoke`) |
| `Data/` | Definitions and the JSON loader | `GBDataTypes.h`, `UGBDataSubsystem` |
| `Stats/` | Stats + modifiers, health/mana | `UGBStatsComponent`, `UGBAttributeComponent` |
| `Combat/` | Damage (one path, one global `OnDamageDealt` event), status effects, projectile, explosion shockwave | `UGBCombatLibrary`, `UGBStatusEffectComponent`, `AGBProjectile`, `AGBExplosionEffect` |
| `Player/` | Character, controller, input | `AGBPlayerCharacter`, `AGBPlayerController`, `UGBInputSet` |
| `Weapons/` | Held items and slots | `UGBEquipmentComponent`, `AGBHeldItem`, `AGBStaff`, `AGBGun`, `AGBSword` |
| `Spells/` | Spellbook, cast resolution, behaviors | `UGBSpellbookComponent`, `FGBSpellCast`, `AGBSpellActor`, `AGBSpell_*` |
| `QTE/` | Quick-time event | `FGBQTESession`, `FGBGestureRecognizer`, `UGBQTEComponent` |
| `World/` | Eras, progress, interactables, test arena | `UGBEraSubsystem`, `UGBEraComponent`, `UGBProgressSubsystem`, `IGBInteractable`, `AGBPortal`, `AGBChest`, `AGBPickup`, `AGBCheckpointVolume`, `AGBTestArena` |
| `AI/` | Enemies (navmesh path, local steering fallback, stuck check) and encounters | `AGBEnemyCharacter`, `GBSteering` (pure decision, tested), `AGBEncounter` |
| `Items/` | Inventory, consumables, armor, recipes | `UGBInventoryComponent` |
| `Progression/` | Skill trees | `UGBSkillTreeComponent` |
| `UI/` | Canvas HUD (two skins), menus, pixel sprites | `AGBHUD`, `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary` |
| `Tests/` | Pure-logic automation tests | `Glyphbound.<Area>.<Name>` |

## Data files (`Glyphbound/Content/Data`)
`Player.json`, `QTE.json`, `Game.json`, `Spells.json`, `Weapons.json`, `StatusEffects.json`, `Items.json` (items + recipes), `Enemies.json`, `Encounters.json`, `Skills.json`, `Sprites.json`. Schemas are the structs in `Data/GBDataTypes.h` (field name = JSON key). Stat and parameter names are the constants in `Core/GBStatNames.h`.

Modifier keys: an actor stat (`MoveSpeed`), `Weapon.<Id>.<Stat>`, `Weapon.<Slot>.<Stat>` (`Weapon.Staff`, `Weapon.Gun`, `Weapon.Sword`), `Weapon.All.<Stat>`, `Spell.<Id>.<Param>`, `Spell.All.<Param>`, `QTE.TimeDilation`...

Standard status effect ids (defined in `StatusEffects.json`, referenced from other files): `Burn`, `Shock`, `Slow`, `Chill`, `HealthPotion`, `ManaPotion`, `HealthInjection`, `Enchant_Fire`, `Enchant_Lightning`, `Enchant_Ice`.

## How the main flows run
- **Cast:** input -> `UGBSpellbookComponent::TryCastSlot` (checks staff in hand, known, cooldown, mana; spends mana) -> `UGBQTEComponent::StartQTE` (slow time, sequence = power, gesture = reach; or instant when off) -> `GBSpell::ResolveCast` (data -> QTE scaling -> modifiers) -> spawn the behavior actor -> it deals damage through `UGBCombatLibrary`.
- **Shoot:** input -> `AGBGun` (fire interval, magazine, spread, recoil, pellets; every number via `GetStat`) -> hitscan -> headshot and distance falloff math in `UGBCombatLibrary` -> `DealDamage`.
- **Era travel:** `AGBPortal::Interact` -> `UGBEraSubsystem::RequestTravel` (fade out, swap era for `UGBEraComponent` actors and `_Past` / `_Future` sub-levels, teleport, restore health/mana/ammo, save checkpoint, fade in).
- **Progress:** encounters set flags in `UGBProgressSubsystem` when cleared; `UGBEraComponent` reads flags, which is how era-gated zones and past-to-future unlocks are built. Death restores the last checkpoint snapshot; flags are never rolled back (enemies do not respawn).
- **Upgrades:** `UGBSkillTreeComponent::Unlock` adds the node's modifiers to the player's stats; weapons and spells pick them up on their next read.

## Conventions
- Game text in English. Code comments in English. ASCII only in source files.
- Native multicast delegates (C++ project; no Blueprint graphs needed).
- No custom collision channels: projectiles and queries use the default channels and filter by team in code.
- Pointers to definitions are not kept across frames (data can be reloaded): keep the id, look it up.
- Tests: only pure logic that is easy to break and hard to see by playing; each one must be able to fail; names `Glyphbound.<Area>.<Name>` where a name is never also a prefix of another.
- Build: `powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` (Editor closed). One build at a time per machine.
